title: Multi-tenant route & model charge decomposer for billing/console
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: produce a per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency decomposition that is accurate enough for console breakdowns and cost chargebacks while remaining operationally cheap to compute at scale. This ticket builds a streaming decomposition service that consumes existing inference telemetry (request traces, batch metadata, KV cache events) and emits attributed rows suitable for the console and chargeback pipeline. Key differentiators: (1) attribution of batched GPU work across multiple logical requests using deterministic token-level apportionment; (2) explicit handling of KV cache hits and prefix reuse so cache-saved tokens are not charged; (3) quantized/adaptive approximation for very large batches to bound compute; (4) multi-tenant fairness heuristics for shared dedicated capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Service ingests production telemetry topic and produces attributed rows for 100% of compatible events within SLA (end-to-end processing < 60s for 95th percentile)
Per-output row must include: timestamp, route_id, model_id, customer_id, token_count, attributed_gpu_ms, attributed_cost_usd, kv_cache_saved_tokens, batch_size, allocation_method
Decomposition must match nightly Monte Carlo job within 1.5% on average for sampled high-volume routes (validation harness included)
Console shows new breakdown card with model-level and customer-level totals in staging (QA dashboard: console/usage/cost-breakdown-staging)
Backfill path exists for last 30 days using map-reduce job if streaming consumer was unavailable
tasks: Design schema for attributed row and register in telemetry catalog
Implement streaming consumer for telemetry.kafka.inference-traces (kafka consumer group: cost-decomposer-v1)
Build deterministic apportionment module that splits GPU-ms and token-cost across requests in a batch
Hook KV-cache event join to avoid charging cached tokens
Add unit + integration tests and validation harness (sample compare to offline Monte Carlo)
Deploy staging consumer, run smoke tests on top-50 routes, iterate on edge cases
Add rollback and backfill job; document in ops runbook
infra_impacts: New Kafka consumer group at high throughput (peak 15k messages/sec); intermediate RocksDB state per-partition to aggregate batch attribution; output stream to telemetry.attributed-costs -> downstream ClickHouse/BigQuery. Requires +2 CPU, +16GB RAM for autoscaling pods, and retention policy on attributed topic of 90 days. Backfill job uses Dataflow/Beam and writes to staging ClickHouse table.
decisions: Use deterministic token-weighted apportionment instead of equal-split to better reflect compute proportionality
Approximate allocation for batches > 1024 tokens using reservoir sampling + linear projection to maintain bounded latency
Emit attributed rows at request granularity (one row per logical request) to keep console joins simple
Keep allocation of cold-start/init overhead as explicit field (init_gpu_ms) rather than amortizing across requests by default
progress_comments: 2025-02-06 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to streamed attribution for text gen + chat routes only. Agreed to exclude embeddings in first pass.
2025-02-12 - Prototype: deterministic apportioner implemented and tested on synthetic batch logs. Early results show <2% error vs ground truth on small samples.
2025-02-20 - Blocker: schema change on telemetry.trace v3 (added batch_token_map) — coordinated with ENG-31245 to add compatibility layer. Assigned to Morgan Lee for adapter.
2025-02-25 - Review feedback from PM (Sophie Martinez): add customer-facing rounding rules and a note about shared GPU amortization. Added acceptance criteria item.
2025-03-01 - Performance tuning: replaced in-memory map with RocksDB-backed window to reduce GC pressure; CPU down from 4.8 -> 3.2 cores in staging tests.

2025-03-04 - QA: smoke run on top-50 routes completed; observed outlier route with heavy KV reuse (route_98) required special handling to credit cache savings to request owner. Created follow-up task to add explicit kv_owner_id join.
Next steps: complete backfill job, add dashboard panels, and enable feature flag for staging console rollout
analytics_schema: Output row fields (CSV/Parquet): [event_ts, window_start_ts, route_id, model_id, customer_id, request_id, tokens_total, tokens_charged, kv_cache_saved_tokens, batch_size, gpu_ms_total, gpu_ms_attributed, init_gpu_ms, attributed_cost_usd, attributed_latency_ms, allocation_method, sample_rate, provenance_tags]
notes: Trade-offs: strict per-token charging increases accuracy for cost recovery but can be expensive to compute at very high QPS; the chosen hybrid approach uses exact apportionment for batches <= 1024 tokens and a fast approximation for larger batches. We considered pushing decomposition to the serving runtime but rejected due to coupling and deployment complexity; the streaming decomposer provides a single source of truth for console + billing and can be iterated independently.
ops_runbook: Staging consumer runs with feature flag 'cost-decomposer.staging=true'. To recover from consumer lag: bump consumer parallelism, run backfill job with date range, and reconcile totals against nightly Monte Carlo report. If attributed topic grows > 200GB/day, enable compressed parquet output and increase retention tier.
qa_playbook: 1) Connect staging console to attributed-costs staging table; 2) Run synthetic generator for 1 hour on top-20 routes at 2x QPS; 3) Compare total attributed_cost_usd against ground truth generator; 4) Verify KV cache credits for cached-only requests
